---
title: "Harmonize historical municipalities"
description: "Map a historical municipality state to a target date and aggregate additive values."
---

<div class="toolbox-kind">Recipe · verified 2026-10-04</div>

## Workflow

```text
historical data + official dated correspondence
  → validate mapping cardinality
  → stop on true splits or unmatched codes
  → join target codes
  → aggregate additive values
  → compare totals before and after
```

This recipe uses `get_geocoding_bfs()` from [Swiss municipalities](../resources/swiss-municipalities.qmd). It handles the common many-old-to-one-target case. It deliberately stops before allocating a true split.

## Retrieve and normalize the key

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(here)

raw_dir <- here("input", "raw")
processed_dir <- here("input", "processed")

bfs_key_raw <- get_geocoding_bfs(
  date1 = "01-01-2020",
  date2 = "01-06-2023",
  raw_path = file.path(
    raw_dir,
    "bfs_correspondence_2020-01-01_2023-06-01.csv"
  )
) |>
  clean_names()

bfs_key <- bfs_key_raw |>
  transmute(
    source_code = initial_code,
    source_name = initial_name,
    target_code = terminal_code,
    target_name = terminal_name
  ) |>
  distinct()
```

Keep codes as character columns. Convert the historical dataset's municipality code to character before joining.

## Diagnose the relationship

```r
duplicate_relations <- bfs_key |>
  count(source_code, target_code) |>
  filter(n > 1)

splits <- bfs_key |>
  distinct(source_code, target_code) |>
  count(source_code, name = "n_targets") |>
  filter(n_targets > 1) |>
  left_join(bfs_key, by = "source_code") |>
  arrange(source_code, target_code)

many_to_one <- bfs_key |>
  distinct(source_code, target_code) |>
  count(target_code, name = "n_sources") |>
  filter(n_sources > 1) |>
  arrange(desc(n_sources))

duplicate_relations
splits
many_to_one

if (nrow(splits) > 0) {
  stop("True municipality splits require an explicit manual allocation rule")
}
```

Many-to-one mappings are expected and can be aggregated. One source code mapping to several target codes is not resolved automatically.

## Join historical data

Assume `df` contains one or more observations per historical municipality and year.

```r
df <- df |>
  mutate(source_code = as.character(municipality_code))

unmatched <- df |>
  distinct(source_code) |>
  anti_join(bfs_key, by = "source_code")

if (nrow(unmatched) > 0) {
  print(unmatched)
  stop("Some source municipality codes have no target correspondence")
}

df_mapped <- df |>
  left_join(
    bfs_key |> select(source_code, target_code, target_name),
    by = "source_code",
    relationship = "many-to-one"
  )
```

`relationship = "many-to-one"` requires a recent dplyr and makes accidental duplicate key rows fail loudly.

## Aggregate additive measures

Name additive columns explicitly. Do not sum rates, percentages, medians or indices. If possible, aggregate their numerators and denominators and recalculate afterward.

```r
additive_values <- c("population", "jobs")

totals_before <- df_mapped |>
  summarise(across(all_of(additive_values), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  mutate(stage = "before")

df_harmonized <- df_mapped |>
  group_by(year, target_code, target_name) |>
  summarise(
    across(all_of(additive_values), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    source_municipalities = n_distinct(source_code),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

totals_after <- df_harmonized |>
  summarise(across(all_of(additive_values), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  mutate(stage = "after")

bind_rows(totals_before, totals_after) |>
  select(stage, everything())
```

If the dataset contains several years or categories, compare totals within every grouping dimension that should be preserved, not only across the entire table.

## Save the reusable target-state data

```r
readr::write_csv(
  df_harmonized,
  file.path(processed_dir, "population_jobs_communes_state_2023-06-01.csv"),
  na = ""
)
```

Record both municipality dates in the analysis. A target-state code is not meaningful without its reference date.
